issues.description: Constructor parameter mismatch for Animal: the UML in the problem statement declares a constructor Animal(String, int) (and an age attribute), but the provided solution defines Animal(String) and the template Main instantiates animals with a single String name (e.g., Seal("Clarabelle")). This inconsistency will confuse students about whether they must implement an age field and a two-parameter constructor for Animal and for subclasses.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor specification consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the UML and problem text to require only a single-parameter constructor Animal(String) (remove the age attribute), and keep the template Main and solution as-is; or (B) update the template and solution to include the age attribute and two-parameter constructors for Animal and all subclasses, and adjust Main to instantiate animals with both name and age.

issues.description: Attribute mismatch for Animal: the UML in the problem statement declares an 'age: int' attribute, but the solution's Animal class contains only 'name' and no 'age' field or related getter/setter. The template's Main also uses only single-argument constructors for animals. Students may be unsure whether they must implement the age attribute and associated constructor/ accessors.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the attribute specification with the implementation and template. Either (A) remove 'age' from the UML and any textual requirements so that only 'name' is required, or (B) add 'age: int' to the Animal implementation (with constructor parameter, getter and setter) and update the template Main and subclass constructors to accept and pass the age.
